body.heading: Why Stone Island sells fast on Vinted
paragraphs: Stone Island is one of the highest-value brands on Vinted UK — and one of the fastest-moving. A standard Stone Island crewneck or hoodie retails at £150–£300 and sells on Vinted for £60–£150 within hours of listing. The most sought-after pieces — Shadow Project jackets, Ghost pieces, vintage compass-patch crewnecks from the 80s and 90s — can sell for £200–£500 and are gone within minutes.

The demand comes from a dedicated collector community (Stone Island collectors, often called 'Stone Island heads') plus streetwear resellers. The brand's scarcity model — limited pieces per season, numbered production, experimental fabrics (heat-reactive, garment-dyed, reflective) — creates permanent second-hand demand. A rare piece listed by someone who doesn't know its value is a major find.

Demand is steady year-round but spikes in autumn/winter (heavyweight pieces — jackets, knits, puffers) and around seasonal drops when new collections drive interest in older pieces. Vintage pieces from the 80s and 90s with the original compass patch are the most valuable and the rarest.

body.heading: Setting up precise Stone Island alerts
paragraphs: Stone Island has a confusing range of lines and most sellers list by piece type and patch rather than collection. A broad 'Stone Island' search returns everything from caps and keyrings to kids' pieces — narrow your alerts.

For the most valuable pieces, set individual alerts: 'Stone Island Shadow Project', 'Stone Island Ghost', 'Stone Island vintage', 'Stone Island compass', 'Stone Island knit', 'Stone Island jacket'. Add your size — Stone Island runs small (size L fits like an M), so most buyers hunt for L and XL. Add price caps based on piece type: £80–£150 for standard crewnecks and hoodies, £150–£300 for jackets, no cap for rare Shadow Project and vintage pieces.

For collector-grade finds, add specific keywords: 'Stone Island reflective', 'Stone Island ice jacket', 'Stone Island heat reactive', 'Stone Island garment dyed', 'Stone Island rare'. These experimental-fabric pieces are the most valuable and the most often mispriced by sellers who don't know what they have.

Check the line under the patch — Stone Island pieces have the season and collection codes on the internal label. If the listing shows the label, you can verify which line and season it is. A Shadow Project piece with the correct labels is worth significantly more than a standard mainline piece.

body.heading: Spotting fake Stone Island on Vinted
paragraphs: Stone Island is one of the most counterfeited brands in the UK — fake pieces are everywhere, and some are very convincing. An alert gets you to the listing first, but you still need to verify authenticity before buying.

The compass patch is the #1 tell. Genuine Stone Island compass patches have a specific design: the compass rose has distinct, well-defined points, the green/red/black/yellow colourway is correct, and the stitching is even and detailed. Fakes often have blurry or slightly-off compass designs, wrong colours, or sloppy stitching. The patch on genuine jackets is also positioned at a specific spot on the left sleeve — fakes often place it incorrectly.

Check the internal labels. Genuine Stone Island pieces have a specific label layout: the main brand label, the season code (e.g. 'SS24' or a numeric code), the 'Stone Island' printed label with the collection name, and the fabric composition label. The style/season codes can be cross-checked online. Fakes often have generic labels, missing season codes, or wrong fonts.

Check the fabric and construction. Stone Island is known for its experimental fabrics — genuine pieces feel substantial, with unique textures (garment-dyed cotton, heat-reactive nylon, reflective materials). Fakes feel thin and generic. Check the zippers — genuine pieces use quality zippers (often branded or from specific suppliers), fakes use cheap unbranded zips.

Finally, check the seller. A seller with multiple Stone Island pieces in different sizes at consistently low prices is almost certainly moving fakes. A one-off listing from a collector clearing out their wardrobe is far more likely to be genuine. When in doubt, post the listing photos in a Stone Island authentication group on Facebook — the community is experienced at spotting fakes.

body.heading: Shadow Project, Ghost, and other lines explained
paragraphs: Stone Island's range confuses even experienced buyers, but knowing the lines helps you spot the valuable pieces. Mainline is the standard collection — the everyday crewnecks, hoodies, jackets, and knits with the compass patch. It's the most common on Vinted and the easiest to buy and resell.

Shadow Project is Stone Island's higher-end technical line — more experimental, more limited, and significantly more valuable. Shadow Project pieces (often with the removable arm pocket, technical fabrics, and minimal branding) command 2–3x the price of equivalent mainline pieces. Set a dedicated alert for 'Shadow Project' with no price cap — they appear rarely and sell in minutes.

Ghost is the monochrome line — all-black pieces with tonal patches (the compass patch is printed in the same colour as the fabric rather than the classic green/red). Ghost pieces are highly sought-after by collectors and hold value extremely well. Search 'Stone Island Ghost' with a high price cap.

Vintage pieces from the 80s and 90s — before the brand's mid-2000s streetwear explosion — are the collector gold. The original compass patches from this era differ from modern ones (slightly different design and materials). A genuine 1990s Stone Island crewneck in good condition can sell for £150–£400. These are the rarest finds on Vinted — set a dedicated vintage alert and check it daily.

body.heading: What to do when your alert fires
paragraphs: Stone Island sells faster than almost any brand on Vinted. When an alert fires, open the listing immediately and check: the compass patch (correct design, colourway, and placement?), the internal labels (season code present and legible?), the fabric and zippers (quality construction?), and any damage (pilling on knits, cracked patch stitching, staining).

If the listing matches your search and looks genuine, buy immediately — don't message the seller asking questions. By the time they reply, a well-priced piece is gone. Vinted doesn't hold items for anyone. Trust your alert filters and your authenticity check.

For high-value pieces (£150+), it's worth double-checking authenticity after buying — post the photos in a Stone Island authentication group on Facebook or the Stone Island subreddit. Vinted's Buyer Protection covers items that don't match the description, so a confirmed fake can be returned.
If a listing is missing photos of the patch and labels, ask the seller for them before buying — for a £200 Shadow Project jacket, the patch and label photos are essential.

faq.question: Which Stone Island pieces sell fastest on Vinted?
faq.answer: Crewnecks, hoodies, and knitwear sell fastest because they have the most inventory and demand. Shadow Project, Ghost, and vintage 80s/90s pieces are rarer and more valuable but appear less frequently — alert catching is essential for those.

faq.question: How do I spot a fake Stone Island compass patch?
faq.answer: Genuine patches have a crisp, detailed compass rose with correct colours (green/red/black/yellow) and even stitching. Fakes have blurry or off-colour compass designs and sloppy stitching. The patch placement on the left sleeve is also a tell — genuine placement is specific and consistent.

faq.question: What's a fair price for Stone Island on Vinted?
faq.answer: Standard crewnecks and hoodies: £60–£150. Jackets: £150–£300. Shadow Project and Ghost pieces: £200–£500+. Vintage 80s/90s pieces: £150–£400. Prices vary hugely by line, condition, and rarity — check the internal labels to identify the line before you buy.

faq.question: Does Supervint log into my Vinted account or auto-buy Stone Island?
faq.answer: No. Supervint is alert-only — it does not log into your Vinted account, does not access your credentials, and does not auto-buy anything. It simply monitors new listings matching your saved searches and sends you an instant notification. You always review and buy manually.

faq.question: What should I check before buying a Shadow Project piece on Vinted?
faq.answer: Photos of the compass patch and internal labels are essential — they confirm the line and season. Check for the removable arm pocket (a Shadow Project signature), quality zippers, and any damage. Ask for extra photos if they're missing, and buy quickly if the listing checks out — Shadow Project pieces sell in minutes.
